verses.greek: Ἦν δέ τις ἀσθενῶν, Λάζαρος ἀπὸ Βηθανίας ἐκ τῆς κώμης Μαρίας καὶ Μάρθας τῆς ἀδελφῆς αὐτῆς.
verses.literal: Was now a certain man ailing Lazarus of Bethany of the village of Mary and Martha the sister of her
verses.dgt: Now a certain man was sick, Lazarus from Bethany, the village of Mary and her sister Martha.

verses.greek: ἦν δὲ Μαριὰμ ἡ ἀλείψασα τὸν κύριον μύρῳ καὶ ἐκμάξασα τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ ταῖς θριξὶν αὐτῆς, ἧς ὁ ἀδελφὸς Λάζαρος ἠσθένει.
verses.literal: Was now Mary the one having anointed the Lord with fragrant oil and having wiped the feet of Him with the hair of her whose the brother Lazarus was sick.
verses.dgt: It was Mary who anointed the Lord with fragrant oil and wiped his feet with her hair; her brother Lazarus was sick.

verses.greek: ἀπέστειλαν οὖν αἱ ἀδελφαὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγουσαι· Κύριε, ἴδε ὃν φιλεῖς ἀσθενεῖ.
verses.literal: Sent therefore the sisters to Him saying Lord behold he whom You love was being sick.
verses.dgt: So the sisters sent to him, saying, “Lord, look, the one you love is sick.”

verses.greek: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Αὕτη ἡ ἀσθένεια οὐκ ἔστιν πρὸς θάνατον ἀλλʼ ὑπὲρ τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ ἵνα δοξασθῇ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ διʼ αὐτῆς.
verses.literal: Having heard then the Jesus said This the sickness not is unto death but for the glory the of God that may be glorified the Son the of God through it.
verses.dgt: But when Jesus heard it, he said, “This sickness is not for death, but for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.”

verses.greek: ἠγάπα δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν Μάρθαν καὶ τὴν ἀδελφὴν αὐτῆς καὶ τὸν Λάζαρον.
verses.literal: was loving now the Jesus the Martha and the sister of her and the Lazarus.
verses.dgt: Now Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.

verses.greek: ὡς οὖν ἤκουσεν ὅτι ἀσθενεῖ, τότε μὲν ἔμεινεν ἐν ᾧ ἦν τόπῳ δύο ἡμέρας·
verses.literal: When therefore He heard that he is sick then indeed He remained in which He was the place two days.
verses.dgt: So when he heard that Lazarus was sick, he then remained two days in the place where he was.

verses.greek: ἔπειτα μετὰ τοῦτο λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς· Ἄγωμεν εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν πάλιν.
verses.literal: Then after this He says to the disciples Let us go into the Judea again.
verses.dgt: Then after this he says to the disciples, “Let us go into Judea again.”

verses.greek: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταί· Ῥαββί, νῦν ἐζήτουν σε λιθάσαι οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι, καὶ πάλιν ὑπάγεις ἐκεῖ;
verses.literal: Say to Him the disciples Rabbi just now were seeking You to stone the Jews and again You are going there?
verses.dgt: The disciples say to him, “Rabbi, just now the Jews were seeking to stone you, and you are going there again?”

verses.greek: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς· Οὐχὶ δώδεκα ὧραί εἰσιν τῆς ἡμέρας; ἐάν τις περιπατῇ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ, οὐ προσκόπτει, ὅτι τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου τούτου βλέπει·
verses.literal: Answered Jesus Surely twelve hours are there in the day? If anyone shall walk in the day not he stumbles because the light of the world this he sees.
verses.dgt: Jesus answered, “Are there not twelve hours in the day? If anyone walks in the day, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world.

verses.greek: ἐὰν δέ τις περιπατῇ ἐν τῇ νυκτί, προσκόπτει, ὅτι τὸ φῶς οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν αὐτῷ.
verses.literal: if however anyone shall walk in the night he stumbles because the light not is in him.
verses.dgt: But if anyone walks in the night, he stumbles, because the light is not in him.”

verses.greek: ταῦτα εἶπεν, καὶ μετὰ τοῦτο λέγει αὐτοῖς· Λάζαρος ὁ φίλος ἡμῶν κεκοίμηται, ἀλλὰ πορεύομαι ἵνα ἐξυπνίσω αὐτόν.
verses.literal: These things He said and after this He says to them Lazarus the friend of us has fallen asleep but I go that I may awaken him.
verses.dgt: He said these things, and after this he says to them, “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going so that I may awaken him.”

verses.greek: εἶπαν οὖν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτῷ· Κύριε, εἰ κεκοίμηται σωθήσεται.
verses.literal: Said therefore the disciples to Him Lord if he has fallen asleep he will get well.
verses.dgt: So the disciples said to him, “Lord, if he has fallen asleep, he will recover.”

verses.greek: εἰρήκει δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς περὶ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ. ἐκεῖνοι δὲ ἔδοξαν ὅτι περὶ τῆς κοιμήσεως τοῦ ὕπνου λέγει.
verses.literal: Had spoken however the Jesus of the death of him they however thought that of the rest the of sleep He speaks.
verses.dgt: But Jesus had spoken about his death, while they thought that he was speaking about the rest of sleep.

verses.greek: τότε οὖν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς παρρησίᾳ· Λάζαρος ἀπέθανεν,
verses.literal: Then therefore said to them the Jesus plainly Lazarus has died.
verses.dgt: Then Jesus told them plainly, “Lazarus has died,

verses.greek: καὶ χαίρω διʼ ὑμᾶς, ἵνα πιστεύσητε, ὅτι οὐκ ἤμην ἐκεῖ· ἀλλὰ ἄγωμεν πρὸς αὐτόν.
verses.literal: And I rejoice for sake of you in order that you may believe that not I was there But let us go to him.
verses.dgt: and for your sake I rejoice that I was not there, so that you may believe. But let us go to him.”

verses.greek: εἶπεν οὖν Θωμᾶς ὁ λεγόμενος Δίδυμος τοῖς συμμαθηταῖς· Ἄγωμεν καὶ ἡμεῖς ἵνα ἀποθάνωμεν μετʼ αὐτοῦ.
verses.literal: Said therefore Thomas who is being named Didymus to the fellow disciples Let us go also us that we may die with Him.
verses.dgt: So Thomas, who is called Didymus, said to his fellow disciples, “Let us also go, so that we may die with him.”

verses.greek: Ἐλθὼν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εὗρεν αὐτὸν τέσσαρας ἤδη ἡμέρας ἔχοντα ἐν τῷ μνημείῳ.
verses.literal: Having come therefore the Jesus found him four already days having been in the tomb.
verses.dgt: So when Jesus came, he found that Lazarus had already been in the tomb four days.

verses.greek: ἦν δὲ ἡ Βηθανία ἐγγὺς τῶν Ἱεροσολύμων ὡς ἀπὸ σταδίων δεκαπέντε.
verses.literal: Was now the Bethany near the Jerusalem about away stadia fifteen.
verses.dgt: Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away,

verses.greek: πολλοὶ δὲ ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐληλύθεισαν πρὸς τὴν Μάρθαν καὶ Μαριὰμ ἵνα παραμυθήσωνται αὐτὰς περὶ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ.
verses.literal: Many now of the Jews had come unto the Martha and Mary that they may console them concerning the brother
verses.dgt: and many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to comfort them concerning their brother.

verses.greek: ἡ οὖν Μάρθα ὡς ἤκουσεν ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἔρχεται ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ· Μαρία δὲ ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ ἐκαθέζετο.
verses.literal: the Therefore Martha when she heard that Jesus is coming met with Him Mary however in the house was sitting.
verses.dgt: So when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went to meet him, but Mary was sitting in the house.

verses.greek: εἶπεν οὖν ἡ Μάρθα πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν· Κύριε, εἰ ἦς ὧδε οὐκ ἂν ἀπέθανεν ὁ ἀδελφός μου·
verses.literal: Said then the Martha to the Jesus Lord if You had been here not then would be dead the brother of mine.
verses.dgt: Then Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.

verses.greek: καὶ νῦν οἶδα ὅτι ὅσα ἂν αἰτήσῃ τὸν θεὸν δώσει σοι ὁ θεός.
verses.literal: even now I know that as much as maybe You may ask the God will give You the God.
verses.dgt: And even now I know that whatever you ask of God, God will give you.”

verses.greek: λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀναστήσεται ὁ ἀδελφός σου.
verses.literal: Says to her the Jesus Will rise again the brother of you.
verses.dgt: Jesus says to her, “Your brother will rise.”

verses.greek: λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ Μάρθα· Οἶδα ὅτι ἀναστήσεται ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.
verses.literal: Says to him the Martha I know that he will rise again in the resurrection in the last day.
verses.dgt: Martha says to him, “I know that he will rise in the resurrection on the last day.”

verses.greek: εἶπεν αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἀνάστασις καὶ ἡ ζωή· ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ κἂν ἀποθάνῃ ζήσεται,
verses.literal: Said to her the Jesus I myself am the resurrection and the life the one believing in Me myself even if he shall die he will live
verses.dgt: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. The one who believes in me, even if he dies, will live,

verses.greek: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ζῶν καὶ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ οὐ μὴ ἀποθάνῃ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα· πιστεύεις τοῦτο;
verses.literal: and everyone who is living and believing in Me myself certainly not he shall die to the age. Believe you this?
verses.dgt: and everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”

verses.greek: λέγει αὐτῷ· Ναί, κύριε· ἐγὼ πεπίστευκα ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ὁ εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἐρχόμενος.
verses.literal: She says to Him Yes Lord I myself have believed that You yourself are the Christ the Son the of God the One into the world coming.
verses.dgt: She says to him, “Yes, Lord. I have believed that you are the Christ, the Son of God, the one coming into the world.”

verses.greek: Καὶ τοῦτο εἰποῦσα ἀπῆλθεν καὶ ἐφώνησεν Μαριὰμ τὴν ἀδελφὴν αὐτῆς λάθρᾳ εἰποῦσα· Ὁ διδάσκαλος πάρεστιν καὶ φωνεῖ σε.
verses.literal: And these things having said she went away and she called Mary the sister of her secretly having said The Teacher is come and He calls you.
verses.dgt: And after saying this, she went away and called Mary her sister secretly, saying, “The Teacher is here and is calling you.”

verses.greek: ἐκείνη δὲ ὡς ἤκουσεν ἠγέρθη ταχὺ καὶ ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτόν·
verses.literal: She then when she heard she rose up quickly and was coming to Him.
verses.dgt: When she heard this, she got up quickly and was going to him.

verses.greek: οὔπω δὲ ἐληλύθει ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν κώμην, ἀλλʼ ἦν ἔτι ἐν τῷ τόπῳ ὅπου ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ ἡ Μάρθα.
verses.literal: Not yet now had come the Jesus into the village but was still in the place where met with Him the Martha.
verses.dgt: Now Jesus had not yet come into the village, but was still in the place where Martha had met him.

verses.greek: οἱ οὖν Ἰουδαῖοι οἱ ὄντες μετʼ αὐτῆς ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ καὶ παραμυθούμενοι αὐτήν, ἰδόντες τὴν Μαριὰμ ὅτι ταχέως ἀνέστη καὶ ἐξῆλθεν, ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῇ δόξαντες ὅτι ὑπάγει εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον ἵνα κλαύσῃ ἐκεῖ.
verses.literal: The then Jews who are being with her in the house and consoling her having seen the Mary that soon she rose up and went out followed after her having supposed that she is going to the tomb that she may weep there.
verses.dgt: Then the Jews who were with her in the house and comforting her, seeing that Mary got up quickly and went out, followed her, thinking that she was going to the tomb to weep there.

verses.greek: ἡ οὖν Μαριὰμ ὡς ἦλθεν ὅπου ἦν Ἰησοῦς ἰδοῦσα αὐτὸν ἔπεσεν αὐτοῦ πρὸς τοὺς πόδας, λέγουσα αὐτῷ· Κύριε, εἰ ἦς ὧδε οὐκ ἄν μου ἀπέθανεν ὁ ἀδελφός.
verses.literal: the Therefore Mary when she came to where was Jesus having seen Him she fell of Him at the feet saying to Him Lord if You had been here not then would my have died the brother.
verses.dgt: So when Mary came to where Jesus was and saw him, she fell at his feet, saying to him, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.”

verses.greek: Ἰησοῦς οὖν ὡς εἶδεν αὐτὴν κλαίουσαν καὶ τοὺς συνελθόντας αὐτῇ Ἰουδαίους κλαίοντας ἐνεβριμήσατο τῷ πνεύματι καὶ ἐτάραξεν ἑαυτόν,
verses.literal: Jesus therefore when He saw her weeping and the having come with her Jews weeping He was deeply moved the in spirit and troubled Himself
verses.dgt: Then Jesus, when he saw her weeping and the Jews who had come with her weeping, was deeply moved in spirit and troubled himself,

verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν· Ποῦ τεθείκατε αὐτόν; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἔρχου καὶ ἴδε.
verses.literal: And He said Where have you laid him? They say to Him Lord do come and do see.
verses.dgt: and he said, “Where have you laid him?” They say to him, “Lord, come and see.”

verses.greek: ἐδάκρυσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς.
verses.literal: Wept the Jesus.
verses.dgt: Jesus wept.

verses.greek: ἔλεγον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι· Ἴδε πῶς ἐφίλει αὐτόν.
verses.literal: Were saying therefore the Jews Behold how He was loving him!
verses.dgt: So the Jews were saying, “See how he loved him!”

verses.greek: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶπαν· Οὐκ ἐδύνατο οὗτος ὁ ἀνοίξας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ τυφλοῦ ποιῆσαι ἵνα καὶ οὗτος μὴ ἀποθάνῃ;
verses.literal: Some however of them said Surely was able this man who having opened the eyes of the blind to have caused that also this one not may have died?
verses.dgt: But some of them said, “Could not this man, who opened the eyes of the blind man, have kept this man also from dying?”

verses.greek: Ἰησοῦς οὖν πάλιν ἐμβριμώμενος ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἔρχεται εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον· ἦν δὲ σπήλαιον, καὶ λίθος ἐπέκειτο ἐπʼ αὐτῷ.
verses.literal: Jesus therefore again being deeply moved in Himself He comes to the tomb It was now a cave and a stone was lying against it.
verses.dgt: Then Jesus, again deeply moved within himself, comes to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone was lying against it.

verses.greek: λέγει ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἄρατε τὸν λίθον. λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ ἀδελφὴ τοῦ τετελευτηκότος Μάρθα· Κύριε, ἤδη ὄζει, τεταρταῖος γάρ ἐστιν.
verses.literal: Says the Jesus do take away the stone. Says to Him the sister of the one having deceased Martha Lord already he stinks four days for it is.
verses.dgt: Jesus says, “Take away the stone.” Martha, the sister of the man who had died, says to him, “Lord, by now there is an odor, for it is the fourth day.”

verses.greek: λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐκ εἶπόν σοι ὅτι ἐὰν πιστεύσῃς ὄψῃ τὴν δόξαν τοῦ θεοῦ;
verses.literal: Says to her the Jesus Surely I said to you that if you shall believe you will see the glory the of God?
verses.dgt: Jesus says to her, “Did I not tell you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?”

verses.greek: ἦραν οὖν τὸν λίθον. ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἦρεν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἄνω καὶ εἶπεν· Πάτερ, εὐχαριστῶ σοι ὅτι ἤκουσάς μου,
verses.literal: They took away therefore the stone where Now Jesus lifted the His eyes upwards and said Father I thank You that You have heard Me.
verses.dgt: So they took away the stone. Then Jesus lifted his eyes upward and said, “Father, I thank you that you heard me.

verses.greek: ἐγὼ δὲ ᾔδειν ὅτι πάντοτέ μου ἀκούεις· ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον τὸν περιεστῶτα εἶπον, ἵνα πιστεύσωσιν ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας.
verses.literal: I myself and knew that always Me You hear but on account of the crowd which already standing around I said it that they may believe that You yourself Me sent.
verses.dgt: I knew that you always hear me, but I said it because of the crowd standing around, so that they may believe that you sent me.”

verses.greek: καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἐκραύγασεν· Λάζαρε, δεῦρο ἔξω.
verses.literal: And these things having said in a voice loud He cried out Lazarus come forth.
verses.dgt: And after saying these things, he cried out with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”

verses.greek: ἐξῆλθεν ὁ τεθνηκὼς δεδεμένος τοὺς πόδας καὶ τὰς χεῖρας κειρίαις, καὶ ἡ ὄψις αὐτοῦ σουδαρίῳ περιεδέδετο. λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Λύσατε αὐτὸν καὶ ἄφετε αὐτὸν ὑπάγειν.
verses.literal: Came forth the one having died bound the feet and the hands with linen strips and the face of him in a headcloth had bound about. Says to them the Jesus: do unbind him and do allow him to go.
verses.dgt: The man who had died came out, his feet and hands bound with burial cloths, and his face wrapped with a cloth. Jesus says to them, “Untie him and let him go.”

verses.greek: Πολλοὶ οὖν ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων, οἱ ἐλθόντες πρὸς τὴν Μαριὰμ καὶ θεασάμενοι ἃ ἐποίησεν, ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτόν·
verses.literal: Many therefore of the Jews the having come to the Mary and having seen what things He did believed in Him.
verses.dgt: Therefore many of the Jews who had come to Mary and had seen what he did believed in him.

verses.greek: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀπῆλθον πρὸς τοὺς Φαρισαίους καὶ εἶπαν αὐτοῖς ἃ ἐποίησεν Ἰησοῦς.
verses.literal: some however of them went to the Pharisees and told to them what did Jesus.
verses.dgt: But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.

verses.greek: συνήγαγον οὖν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συνέδριον, καὶ ἔλεγον· Τί ποιοῦμεν ὅτι οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος πολλὰ ποιεῖ σημεῖα;
verses.literal: Gathered therefore the chief priests and the Pharisees a council and they were saying What are we to do? For this the man many does signs!
verses.dgt: So the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered a council and were saying, “What are we doing? This man is doing many signs.

verses.greek: ἐὰν ἀφῶμεν αὐτὸν οὕτως, πάντες πιστεύσουσιν εἰς αὐτόν, καὶ ἐλεύσονται οἱ Ῥωμαῖοι καὶ ἀροῦσιν ἡμῶν καὶ τὸν τόπον καὶ τὸ ἔθνος.
verses.literal: If we shall let him alone Him like this all will believe in Him and will come the Romans and will take away of us both the place and the nation.
verses.dgt: If we leave him this way, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.”

verses.greek: εἷς δέ τις ἐξ αὐτῶν Καϊάφας, ἀρχιερεὺς ὢν τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ἐκείνου, εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε οὐδέν,
verses.literal: One however certain of them Caiaphas high priest being on the year same said to them You yourselves not know no thing
verses.dgt: But one of them, Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, said to them, “You know nothing at all,

verses.greek: οὐδὲ λογίζεσθε ὅτι συμφέρει ὑμῖν ἵνα εἷς ἄνθρωπος ἀποθάνῃ ὑπὲρ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ ἔθνος ἀπόληται.
verses.literal: nor consider you that it is profitable for you that one man may die for the people and not all the nation may perish.
verses.dgt: nor do you consider that it is better for you that one man die for the people and that the whole nation not perish.”

verses.greek: τοῦτο δὲ ἀφʼ ἑαυτοῦ οὐκ εἶπεν, ἀλλὰ ἀρχιερεὺς ὢν τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ἐκείνου ἐπροφήτευσεν ὅτι ἔμελλεν Ἰησοῦς ἀποθνῄσκειν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἔθνους,
verses.literal: This now from himself not he said but high priest being on the year that he prophesied that was about Jesus to die for the nation
verses.dgt: Now he did not say this from himself, but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus was going to die for the nation,

verses.greek: καὶ οὐχ ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἔθνους μόνον, ἀλλʼ ἵνα καὶ τὰ τέκνα τοῦ θεοῦ τὰ διεσκορπισμένα συναγάγῃ εἰς ἕν.
verses.literal: and not for the nation only but that also the children the of God those scattered He may gather together into one.
verses.dgt: and not for the nation only, but also so that he might gather into one the children of God who had been scattered.

verses.greek: ἀπʼ ἐκείνης οὖν τῆς ἡμέρας ἐβουλεύσαντο ἵνα ἀποκτείνωσιν αὐτόν.
verses.literal: From that very therefore the day they plotted that they may kill Him.
verses.dgt: So from that day they planned to kill him.

verses.greek: Ὁ οὖν Ἰησοῦς οὐκέτι παρρησίᾳ περιεπάτει ἐν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις, ἀλλὰ ἀπῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν εἰς τὴν χώραν ἐγγὺς τῆς ἐρήμου, εἰς Ἐφραὶμ λεγομένην πόλιν, κἀκεῖ ἔμεινεν μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν.
verses.literal: the Therefore Jesus no longer publicly was walking among the Jews but went away from there into the region near the wilderness to Ephraim being named a city And there He stayed with the disciples
verses.dgt: Therefore Jesus no longer walked openly among the Jews, but went away from there to the region near the wilderness, to a city called Ephraim, and there he remained with the disciples.

verses.greek: Ἦν δὲ ἐγγὺς τὸ πάσχα τῶν Ἰουδαίων, καὶ ἀνέβησαν πολλοὶ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἐκ τῆς χώρας πρὸ τοῦ πάσχα ἵνα ἁγνίσωσιν ἑαυτούς.
verses.literal: Was now near the Passover of the Jews and went up many to Jerusalem out of the region before the Passover so that they may purify themselves.
verses.dgt: Now the Passover of the Jews was near, and many went up to Jerusalem from the country before the Passover so that they might purify themselves.

verses.greek: ἐζήτουν οὖν τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἔλεγον μετʼ ἀλλήλων ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἑστηκότες· Τί δοκεῖ ὑμῖν; ὅτι οὐ μὴ ἔλθῃ εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν;
verses.literal: They were seeking therefore the Jesus and were saying among one another in the temple already standing What does it seem to you that certainly not He may come to the feast?
verses.dgt: So they were seeking Jesus and were saying to one another as they stood in the temple, “What do you think? Surely he will not come to the feast?”

verses.greek: δεδώκεισαν δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἐντολὰς ἵνα ἐάν τις γνῷ ποῦ ἐστιν μηνύσῃ, ὅπως πιάσωσιν αὐτόν.
verses.literal: Had given now the chief priests and the Pharisees commands that if anyone shall know where He is he shall show it so that they may seize Him.
verses.dgt: Now the chief priests and the Pharisees had given orders that if anyone knew where he was, he should report it, so that they might arrest him.
